name: Performance Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building performance — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary performance tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building performance — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary performance tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep performance changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Prefer explicit, readable performance solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. State assumptions about performance explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Document any non-obvious performance decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Before starting performance work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen performance approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Measure before optimizing any performance bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new performance abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting performance assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop performance edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated performance concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these performance guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
